This pattern is classic for severe inflammatory acne vulgaris, specifically nodulocystic acne, which has led to atrophic and hypertrophic scarring. It could also be a form of folliculitis decalvans, but that usually causes patchy alopecia. Another differential is keratosis pilaris, but that doesn't cause this level of inflammation and scarring. Hidradenitis suppurativa? No, wrong location. So, Acne Vulgaris (Nodulocystic) is #1. Folliculitis is #2. Acne Keloidalis Nuchae is #3 (though usually nape). Discoid Lupus Erythematosus is #4 (can cause scarring alopecia and plaques, but the lesions look more cystic/pustular). Rosacea? Unlikely to have this much scarring. Seborrheic dermatitis? No, that's scaling.
